## Scope of this document {#sec-scope}

`SPEC_f4_ps_effect_gap.md` set four questions and asked for a resolutions
section. That was **narrowed mid-task to questions 1 and 4 only**, with the
resolutions section dropped. This document answers those two and nothing else.

Deliberately **not** here:

- **Q2** — how far apart the adjusted and unadjusted effects are for the
  selected subgroup.
- **Q3** — whether the *ranking* changes: Spearman correlation over the family,
  argmax agreement, and admission-status changes against `c_screen`. This is the
  question that decides whether F4 is a **variance-estimation** problem or a
  **selection** problem, and it is unanswered.
- The three resolutions (extend the influence path / make the docstring true /
  hard-error) and what the evidence says about each.

One behaviour-free change was made: the docstring correction the spec permits
(@sec-docstring). No behaviour was changed.

---

## Verified from source {#sec-source}

Read rather than inferred. Line numbers current as of `917e15d`; where the spec
cited a different number it is noted.

| claim | site | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `ps_method <- if (is.RCT) "none" else "grf"` | `forestsearch_main.R:1892-1893` | **confirmed** |
| `ps_adjust_resolved` set | `:1903` | **confirmed** |
| estimator closure rebuilt with `ps_adjust_method = ps_adjust_resolved` | `:1967-1974` | **confirmed** (spec said `1966-1973`; off by one) |
| `adjust_covariates` mutually exclusive with `ps_method != "none"` | `:1913-1918` | **confirmed** |
| `.consistency_glm_pieces()` has no propensity formal | `consistency_resample.R:221-224` | **confirmed** (spec said `:221`; the function moved when `411a448` added roxygen, but the formals line is still 221) |
| the only measure guard is `IRD` | `consistency_resample.R:230` | **confirmed** |
| `.fs_mr_pieces()` passes no propensity information | `fs_mr_inference.R:61-73` | **confirmed** |

The formals are exactly `df`, `outcome_type`, `effect_measure`, `treat.name`,
`outcome.name`, `offset.name`, `adjust_covariates`, `adverse_outcome`. Grepping
the function body for `sw`, `ps_hat`, `ips_covar`, `weights` or `propensity`
returns nothing.

The `adjust_covariates` guard sharpens the gap exactly as the spec said it
would: in this branch that formal is necessarily `NULL`, so the model fitted is
**fully unadjusted**, not differently adjusted.

---

## Q1 — does MR execute under `ps_method != "none"`? {#sec-q1}

**Yes, fully, and silently.**

ACTG175 binary, OR, `subgroup_method = "consistency"`,
`consistency_method = "resample"`, `mr_inference = TRUE`, 1000 draws.
`is.RCT = FALSE` makes `ps_method` resolve to `"grf"` — the **default** for a
non-randomised analysis, not an exotic setting. (ACTG175 is a randomised trial;
`is.RCT = FALSE` is set to exercise the path, which is what the question asks
about.)

| `is.RCT` | `ps_adjust_method` | resolved `ps_method` | validator fired | MR variant | `n_family` | naive OR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| `TRUE` | (default) | `none` | no | **FULL** | 1450 | 2.982955 |
| `FALSE` | (default → `iptw`) | `grf` | no | **FULL** | 1450 | 2.982955 |
| `FALSE` | `iptw` | `grf` | no | **FULL** | 1450 | 2.982955 |
| `FALSE` | `dr_gcomp` | `grf` | no | **FULL** | 1450 | 2.982955 |

Three things follow.

**`.validate_mr_configuration()` never fires.** Confirmed both by reading —
grepping its body for `ps_method` / `ps_adjust` / `propensity` returns nothing —
and by the runs. It inspects `subgroup_method`, `dina_select_statistic`,
`grf_selection`, `grf_select_statistic`, `use_lasso`, `use_grf` and `use_dina`,
and nothing else. Propensity adjustment is invisible to it.

**MR returns the full variant, not the short one.** There is no `note`, no
degraded family, no fallback. `n_family` is 1450 in every row. Nothing in the
returned object records that the correction describes a different functional
from the one selected on.

**The reported estimate is bit-identical across all four rows.** `2.982955` to
every digit printed, whether PS adjustment is off, IPTW, or g-computation. That
identity is the cleanest available demonstration that the influence path is
blind to the propensity adjustment — not approximately, exactly. Changing
`ps_adjust_method` changes nothing MR reports.

Two qualifications, so the result is not over-read:

- The **selected subgroup is the same** in all four runs
  (`!{cd40 <= 421} & !{wtkg <= 82}`), so the identical naive estimate follows
  from fitting the same unadjusted model to the same rows. What the identity
  demonstrates is the blindness of the influence path, not that the identifier's
  ranking is unaffected. **Whether the ranking changes is Q3, and Q3 was not
  run.** On ACTG175 — a randomised trial, where estimated propensity scores are
  near-constant — the adjustment has little to bite on, and this says nothing
  about data where it would.
- The information is **present but unread**. `fs$df.est` carries `sw`, `ps_hat`
  and `ips_covar`. The influence path is not missing the data; it has no
  argument that would tell it to look.

## Q4 — which paths reach the influence path? {#sec-q4}

Enumerated with unbounded `grep -rn` and counted, per the spec's warning about
`head`-limited searches.

### The influence path itself

`.consistency_glm_pieces()` has **2** live callers (a third hit is a comment):

| site | caller |
|---|---|
| `consistency_resample.R:403` | `consistency_resample()` |
| `fs_mr_inference.R:67` | `.fs_mr_pieces()` |

`.fs_mr_pieces()` has **4** callers:

| site | caller | reaches it when |
|---|---|---|
| `fs_mr_inference.R:96` | `.fs_mr_assemble()` — every candidate in MR's family | `mr_inference = TRUE` |
| `fs_mr_inference.R:482` | `fs_mr_inference()`, complement subgroup | `include_complement = TRUE` (the default) |
| `forestsearch_helpers.R:1133` | `.dina_reselect_on_effect()` | `subgroup_method = "dina"`, `dina_select_statistic = "effect"` (default) |
| `forestsearch_helpers.R:1543` | `.grf_reselect_on_effect()` | `subgroup_method = "grf"`, `grf_select_statistic = "effect"` (default) |

`consistency_resample()` has **5** live callers (plus one comment and one
`exists()` guard):

| site | caller |
|---|---|
| `subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:1453` | `evaluate_subgroup_consistency()`, Cox branch |
| `subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:1474` | `evaluate_subgroup_consistency()`, GLM branch |
| `subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:1825`, `:1829` | `evaluate_consistency_twostage()` |
| `consistency_resample.R:485` | `consistency_resample_compare()` (exported, standalone) |

### Routes on which `ps_method != "none"` coexists with it

| # | route | reached by | PS carried? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MR over the consistency family | `forestsearch(mr_inference = TRUE)` | yes — closure adjusted, influence not |
| 2 | MR's complement subgroup | same, `include_complement = TRUE` | yes |
| 3 | MR on the DINA branch | `subgroup_method = "dina"` | yes |
| 4 | MR on the GRF branch | `subgroup_method = "grf"` | yes |
| 5 | the resample consistency engine | `consistency_method = "resample"` | yes — every candidate's $P_{\text{cons}}$ |
| 6 | the two-stage consistency engine | `use_twostage = TRUE` (default) | yes |
| 7 | every bootstrap replicate | `forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture()` | yes — routes 1–6 replayed per replicate |
| 8 | every CV fold | `forestsearch_Kfold()` / `_tenfold()` | yes — routes 1–6 replayed per fold |
| 9 | `consistency_resample_compare()` | direct call | n/a — takes raw data, no `forestsearch()` config |

Routes 5 and 6 matter as much as 1–4 and are easy to miss: the consistency rate
is computed from the same unadjusted `beta_hat` and `sigma_D`, so under
`ps_method != "none"` the **screen** $t_g$ is applied to a different functional
from the one the identifier ranks on — not only the post-selection correction.

Nothing nulls or guards `ps_method` on the replay paths: the bootstrap does not
mention it, and CV explicitly carries it (`forestsearch_cross_validation.R:395`,
`:885`: "ps_method and ps_adjust_method carry through via args_call_all").

### Exhaustive check on the weight column

Every site in `R/` that reads `sw` — 12 hits, all listed:

- **written** at `forestsearch_main.R:1943` and `glm_effect_estimators.R:1085`;
- **read** only at `glm_effect_estimators.R:235`, `:237`, `:354`, `:355`,
  `:468`, `:473`, `:650`, `:658`, `:830`, `:831` — all inside
  `make_effect_estimator()`'s closures.

No read in `consistency_resample.R`, `fs_mr_inference.R`, `subgroup_search.R` or
`Cox_estimation_helpers.R`. The adjustment lives entirely in the estimator
closure and nowhere in the influence apparatus.

### Two adjacent observations from the enumeration

Neither is F4, and neither was chased. Both were found by enumerating routes and
are recorded so they are not lost.

**Survival plus `ps_method != "none"` appears to be a no-op.** The closure
rebuild at `forestsearch_main.R:1967` is guarded by `if (is_glm)`, and
`estimator_fn` is built only inside `if (outcome_type != "survival")`
(`:1546`, `:1589`), so it is `NULL` for survival. `fit_cox_for_subgroup()`,
`.consistency_cox_pieces()` and `Cox_estimation_helpers.R` contain no `weights`
or `sw` reference. So PS is estimated, the columns are attached, and nothing
consumes them: the survival path is unadjusted throughout while reporting
`ps_method = "grf"`. `make_effect_estimator()` *does* have a weighted Cox branch
(`glm_effect_estimators.R:235-237`), but `forestsearch()` never builds a closure
for survival, so that branch is unreachable from `forestsearch()`.

**The bootstrap carries a user-supplied `ps_hat` into replicates unaligned.**
CV nulls `ps_hat` because it would be "wrong length for training fold"
(`forestsearch_cross_validation.R:394-396`, `:884-886`). The bootstrap nulls
nothing propensity-related, and a bootstrap resample has the **same** row count
as the original — so `forestsearch()`'s length check at `:1922` passes and the
original subjects' propensity scores are used for the resampled rows. This bites
only when the user passes `ps_hat` explicitly; at the default `NULL` the PS is
re-estimated per replicate. Structurally the same conditional shape as F12.

## The docstring correction {#sec-docstring}

Made. The spec permitted it and observed that silently keeping the false claim
is not defensible; it is documentation-only and independent of how F4 resolves.

`R/consistency_resample.R:199-203` said `"IRD"` **and** propensity-adjusted
(`iptw` / `dr_gcomp`) effects "are not single coefficients, so they return
`NULL` (the caller falls back to splitting)". The body's only such guard is
`if (effect_measure == "IRD") return(NULL)`. The claim was not merely false but
**unfulfillable** — the function has no argument from which it could learn it is
in the propensity-adjusted case.

The docstring now states that the function fits an unweighted, unadjusted model;
that `"IRD"` alone returns `NULL`; and, in a dedicated section, that under
`ps_method != "none"` a propensity-adjusted effect is fitted *as if unadjusted*
rather than declined, with the consequence for
$\hat\beta(g)$, $db_{g,i}$, $\sigma_{D,g}$ and the whole correction. It records
that the previous claim was never true, and points here.

**No guard was added**, per the spec. The behaviour is unchanged.

Also corrected: the opening sentence claimed the function "fits the same
treatment-effect model the corresponding `make_effect_estimator()` closure
fits". Under `ps_method != "none"` that is exactly what it does not do, and it
is the same false claim in a weaker form.

---

## What remains open {#sec-open}

- **Q2 and Q3 were not run.** Q3 in particular is load-bearing: it decides
  whether F4 is a variance-estimation problem (the ranking is intact, only the
  correction describes the wrong functional) or a selection problem (the
  identifier and MR disagree about which subgroup won). Those need different
  fixes.
- **The resolutions were not assessed.** Nothing here rules any of the three in
  or out.
- The choice turns on whether the manuscript's scope covers non-randomised data
  at all. Both applications are randomised trials, so it may not — in which case
  the cheapest honest resolution may be the hard error rather than extending the
  influence path.
